Maximum likelihood estimation of local immigration rates \((m_1,...,m_K)\) based on the K-deme sampling formula

Source: R/estimation.R
optim_multideme.Rd

optim_multideme() computes the maximum likelihood estimate for the multi-deme parameters for a given species abundance matrix \((n_{1j}, ..., n_{kj})\) for deme j (\(j\in\{1,...,K\}\)) where \(n_{ij}\) is the number of organisms of species i in deme j and k is the total number of species (for all \(i, n_i \geq 0\)). The formulation in this description is that of species abundance distributions but is valid for any partition in a subdivided setting (e.g., word frequencies in multiple books).

The matrix must have one row per deme and one column per species. The regional species abundance distribution is obtained by summing the demes (rows).

Usage

optim_multideme(
  input_abundance_matrix,
  verbose = FALSE,
  I_max = NULL,
  ci = FALSE,
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

input_abundance_matrix

a matrix \(n_{ij}\) of abundances (one row per deme (local site) j, one column per species i). A data frame of counts is accepted.

verbose

if TRUE, report progress over the demes with message() (default FALSE)

I_max

upper bound of the search interval for I: NULL (default, the deme size J), or a positive number, or one number per deme

ci

if TRUE, also return likelihood-ratio confidence intervals (default FALSE)

level

confidence level of the intervals (default 0.95)

Value

A list with

I

rescaled immigration rate, \(I=\frac{m}{1-m}(J-1)\), a vector of real numbers

m

immigration rate, a vector of real numbers

J

local community size, a vector of integers

k

number of classes/species, a vector of integers

logl

maximal log-likelihood of each deme (up to a constant that does not depend on I), a vector of real numbers

se_I, se_m

standard errors of I and m, vectors of real numbers

ci_I, ci_m

only if ci = TRUE: confidence intervals of I and m, matrices with one row per deme and columns lower and upper

Boundary and degenerate cases

  • A deme with a single individual carries no information on the immigration rate: I and m are NA and a warning is issued.

  • A deme containing a single species has its likelihood maximal at I = 0 (m = 0); this value is returned as is.

  • The search interval for I is [1e-6, I_max] with I_max equal to the deme size J by default. If an estimate lies on the edge of this interval (for instance a deme that is essentially a random sample of the regional pool, for which the likelihood keeps increasing with I), a warning is issued; increase I_max to explore larger values.

Uncertainty

The standard errors se_I and se_m are obtained from the exact second derivative of the log-likelihood in I (and the delta method for m); they are NA when the estimate lies on a bound of the search interval or for a deme with a single species. With ci = TRUE, likelihood-ratio confidence intervals are also returned: the range of I over which the log-likelihood stays within qchisq(level, 1) / 2 of its maximum. A limit equal to a bound of the search interval means that the interval extends at least to that bound. These replace the Std_I and Std_m columns of the TeTame software.

See also

optim_ewens(), optim_pitman(), optim_etienne()

Examples

input_abundances1 <- c(44, 37, 34, 5, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1)
input_abundances2 <- c(240, 20, 48, 2, 21, 1, 3, 2, 5, 2, 0, 1, 1)
input_abundance_matrix <- rbind(input_abundances1, input_abundances2)
optim_multideme(input_abundance_matrix)
#> $I
#> [1]  69.44552 197.91949
#> 
#> $m
#> [1] 0.3363867 0.3645467
#> 
#> $J
#> [1] 138 346
#> 
#> $k
#> [1] 13 12
#> 
#> $logl
#> [1] -255.5496 -392.8408
#> 
#> $se_I
#> [1]  34.80389 128.98987
#> 
#> $se_m
#> [1] 0.1118761 0.1509746
#>
